utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-02-60-T, the Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. McCloskey. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good morning everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. McCloskey: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, yesterday we were just beginning to get into 13 July and some of the documents and intercepts that were part of your continuing narrative into the events and issues. So let's just get right into the next document, and I'll ask you about some of the surrounding events if it seems appropriate. So let's just go to the 459 and tell us what this is and what you find significant about it for the events on those days.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is an interim combat report from the command of the 5th Engineering Battalion of the Drina Corps on 13 July 1995. As I had indicated in my testimony yesterday on prior exhibits, the police forces and particularly the individual Dragomir Vasic had the impression that he was all alone on that particular road stretch and that they were the only forces engaged in the fighting. And as this document indicates, in fact, there were army units not only garrisoned there but were also engaged in some of the combat operations and taking casualties. So this is a document that I used just to set some context that there were other forces not only along the road but in Konjevic Polje and other places. And the combat that occurred on the 13th of July, as we'll get into, was an operation that the army and the police units were both involved in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go on to the next exhibit which is an intercept 206/1 dated 13 July. Tell us about this.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it's Prosecution Exhibit 206, and that's a /A.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: /A. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a 13 July intercept at 1009 hours. The correspondents noted are an individual named Beara and an individual named Lukic. Beara, we understand, is in fact, Colonel Ljubisa Beara of the VRS Main Staff security organ. He is the head of that security organ. In the context of this conversation -- well, just backing up first, this is the first either document or intercept which puts Colonel Beara involved on the ground with respect the issues related to Srebrenica 1995. So from a documentary point of view, this is the first hit that we have on this individual. And as you read through the text of the intercept, it's clear that the issue of discussion is numbers of Bosnian Muslim soldiers who are now showing up in and around the area of Konjevic Polje being disarmed and are being taken prisoner. Approximately three-quarters of the way down the intercept, Colonel Beara is noting that shove them all on the playground, and in that respect I believe this Court has heard testimony that hundreds of Bosnian Muslim prisoners were held at Nova Kasaba at an area we call the football pitch or the soccer field.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there also an aerial image from the 13 of July related to that issue?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, there is. On the second page, as they're talking about numbers of prisoners as well as the numbers of individuals in the column, again halfway down you have references to the fact that there are indications that some of the Bosnian Muslims are killing themselves and that there are also, in fact, plenty of wounded. And towards the bottom, more references to the numbers of prisoners at Konjevic Polje. The third page starts to -- of the intercept starts to get away from the issue of prisoners and starts to go into more topics related to the general political situation with respect to the UN and visits to other places such as Rogatica, Vlasenica. And that is the end of the intercept as we have it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, does Mr. Beara statements indicate in part his -- an attitude towards prisoners?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly from the context of this intercept it indicates an extremely negative attitude towards the prisoners.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which particular statement are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, first on the first page with respect to references that "They're killing themselves," Beara's phrase, "Well, excellent, just let them continue. Fuck it" -- I'm sorry that was the second page. My mistake. On the first page with respect to, "Shove them all on the playground, who gives an fuck about them." And we could probably go through for a few more references, but I believe that gives you the general idea.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go on to the next exhibit. And this is Exhibit 208 and from the 13th at 1355 hours. What's the significance of this?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This particular intercept is the first intercept which I believe specifically relates to the beginnings of the organised mass execution process. It is a discussion between an individual Colonel Milanovic, who was in fact Colonel Ignjat Milanovic, a Drina Corps staff officer and the Palma duty officer. While part of the discussion with Palma is blank, enough exists that you can determine that Colonel Milanovic is inquiring from the Palma duty officer as to the availability of a bulldozer with the scoop and is being informed that for whatever reason it is not available before a certain time. He makes it clear that should one be found, it should report to Konjevic Polje at that time to be there for us. This corresponds in time to testimony that I believe is before the Court with respect to this mass execution which occurs in the Cerska Valley area at approximately 1300 hours on 13 July 1995. If I can relate to the map for a second. This is Konjevic Polje, and the Cerska Valley execution takes place in this area right here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And for the record that was the orange dot just a few kilometres below the village of Cerska. And can you just remind us just the high points of the what we know about the Cerska Valley execution, just very briefly.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The information we have about the Cerska Valley information comes from a witness who witnessed a convoy of three buses led by an armoured personnel carrier and later followed by a piece of engineering equipment, a back hoe, I believe, at the intersection of Konjevic Polje turning down the road that parallels the Cerska River. We don't know much beyond that, in so much as there are no known survivors of the Cerska Valley executions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just very briefly, the mass grave, what did it tell us there at Cerska?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In respect to the mass grave at Cerska, a number of the bodies exhumed, I believe a large portion of them, were exhumed with hands wired behind their backs and it was generally an undisturbed grave. It was not one that was secondary and had been disturbed. I believe Mr. Manning will be coming on and will be able to provide more details about the condition of the bodies. But certainly in a broad level it had all the hallmarks of an execution. It was not a battle casualty related grave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, bulldozers, as noted in this intercept, can be used for legitimate military functions. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any indication of any such military functions occurring at this time involving excavations or bulldozers?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. That is an issue that I specifically checked in reviewing this intercept. I've done a considerable amount of research trying to determine if there was any feasible military alternative or evidence thereof that would relate to this, and I found no evidence to demonstrate that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of any other mass graves in the area of Cerska, Konjevic Polje, Nova Kasaba?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a smaller, well not mass grave in this instance, but there is a smaller execution site that we call the Jadar River execution site that occurred approximately one hour prior to this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did that involve any obvious signs of organisation?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: My understanding of the facts behind that is that a bus pulled up, escorted -- a group of Bosnian Muslims were loaded on the bus, taken to a remote location, and executed. The fact that a bus at that time was pulled out of the general process of continuing to remove the Bosnian Muslims from the Potocari area and was made available for that use is an indication that it was organised at a higher level.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Getting back to -- do you know of -- the bulldozer question, do you know of any mass graves in that area, Konjevic Polje, Nova Kasaba?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, from my understanding, and it's been a while since I've had to do the mass graves part, but certainly the Cerska Valley mass graves, they're -- further on towards Kravica you have the Glogova mass graves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, this 13 July intercept regarding bulldozers, is there another document from Zvornik that we'll get into later that mentions anything along the same lines?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What's that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In an upcoming exhibit where we have the duty logbook of the duty operations officer of the Zvornik Brigade, at approximately the 1300 hour time frame, there will be a remark in that book that reflects bulldozers. I believe that comment is directly related to this conversation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What's the next exhibit we've got?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately two hours later, and Prosecution Exhibit 211, on 13 July, you had the synopsis of a conversation where Milanovic is calling the customs house, which is the location of the headquarters of the 5th Engineer Battalion, asking for Simovic or Avramovic, both whom are the commander and deputy commander. Major Avramovic is the commander of the Engineering Battalion, and as indicated from one of the previous exhibits, Simovic is the deputy commander of the battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe the deputy commander's name was a little different than that.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I can go back to P459, this is the deputy commander Mile Simanic. Again, the topic of conversation is the location or the acquisition of excavators or a bulldozer, being told that the answer is negative, that they're all in use. Going to the second part of the conversation, there is a reference to a Lieutenant Colonel Blagojevic, and I'd just like to note that in this respect I believe the individual that they're talking about is Lieutenant Colonel Nedjo Blagojevic, the Drina Corps communications officer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And what is the next exhibit you set aside?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an intercept between two correspondents at 1730 hours on 13 July 1995. And it's discussing gross numbers of individuals, men -- or basically individuals of military age.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is Exhibit 213.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The correspondents discuss the fact that they're still transporting women and children, and that at various places which are not designated, there are roughly 1500 to 2.000. It does talk later in the conversation about, "Okay, and then I send them and have them report there in Kasaba to the last." Nova Kasaba is indicated as a collection point for Bosnian Muslim taken on 13 July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "And have them report to the stadium," where do you think that refers to?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that's a reference to the football pitch, sir. Also noting an unspecified job with respect to transportation. Is it finished? And they're at the intersection of what I believe is Konjevic Polje/Nova Kasaba road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And what's the next document?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this point in time at 1730 hours on 13 July, as the information that is before the Court, one of the first -- or I shouldn't say first, but one of the most significant incidents that occurs in the area of Bratunac and specifically in the zone of the Bratunac infantry brigade is an event that we call the massacre at the Kravica warehouse. As the Court is aware, over a two-and-a-half-hour period, from approximately 1700 to 1930 hours on 13 July, a number of Bosnian Muslims believed to be between 750 and 1.000 who were being detained at that warehouse were killed. This document --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is Exhibit 464.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is an extract from the entry log of the Bratunac military medical centre, covering the period 13 July 1995 in the afternoon. If you look at entry 1489, it reflects that an individual by the name of Miroslav Stanojevic was admitted at 1730 hours. He was wounded at Kravica. It describes the injury as an entrance and exit wound, and reflects that he is a member of the Red Beret unit. The Red Berets, as you're aware, is an intervention platoon subordinate to the 3rd Battalion of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade. Entry 1490 reflects --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, before we go there, do you have any other information indicating what unit Miroslav Stanojevic belongs to besides this entry?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: We have been able to cross-index his name on a listing of all the soldiers of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade for July of 1995, which of course is part of the records that the OTP has seized, and it, in fact, confirms his association and that he is a member of that unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this medical record, how did the OTP get this medical record?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The OTP obtained this particular medical record in a search of the Bratunac medical centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you recall what eventually the fate of Mr. Stanojevic was?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe the investigation has determined that he died in an auto accident approximately a year to two years ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. If you could go down to the next one then.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is item number 1490, reflecting an individual Rade Cuturic. He came into the medical centre at 1740 hours on 13 July 1995. He is a -- from Sekovici and is identified as a member of the MUP special brigade. In fact, as the information has indicated as part of my report, I don't have it as an exhibit, but Rade Cuturic is in fact the deputy commander of the Sekovici special police detachment. It reflects that he was also wounded at Kravica and he's suffering from burns on the palm of his hand. Closing the book on Mr. Cuturic, within a month he becomes the commander of that detachment and I believe in late August, early September, he is killed in combat on Mount Majevica. Continuing to entry 1491, it indicates the admittance of Krsto Dragicevic, also a member of the special police brigade from Skelani, wounded at Kravica and in fact deceased.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if during these early evening hours of 1730 to 1930, do you know if there was any combat in the area of Kravica from the Muslim column filtering through?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, again because of the dictates of terrain, the route of the column did not come near the actual village of Kravica. It did not come near the road until a point near Sandici a point a few kilometres up the road. The investigation and interviews and the general body of information surrounding the Kravica warehouse clearly indicates that there was no combat activity at that time at that location.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to the next exhibit.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Prosecution Exhibit 465. This is the details of the welfare status of the familiar of Dragicevic, Krsto, reflecting his former organisational unit as a 2nd Detachment from Sekovici. And again, the identification of both those individuals, Mr. Cuturic and Mr. Dragicevic as members of the 2nd Detachment of Sekovici at Kravica is consistent with other information which the investigation has developed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go on to the next exhibit, 466. And tell us what this is.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a Main Staff order that is dated 13 July, and with the Court's indulgence I will be able to demonstrate that by the next exhibit, which is from the Main Staff to the commands of the Drina Corps, the Drina Corps forward command post and a number of the brigades of the Drina Corps, directly to the command or chief of staff personally. This document deals with the prevention of Muslim groups from crossing towards Tuzla and Kladanj and is an order from the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the Bratunac Brigade? I don't see that in the heading?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. It is not directed to them, this particular order, in the heading. However, we are able to determine, and I believe this is the -- a receipt stamp of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade. So while it was not directed to them, they did in fact receive a copy. Given the fact that there was still a Drina Corps IKM at Bratunac, that may very well explain why this copy went through Bratunac. This order directs -- is a component of paragraph 1 that the corps command and brigade commands shall use all available able-bodied manpower in their zones of responsibility in discovering, blocking, disarming, and capturing observed Muslim groups as well as preventing their crossing into Muslim-controlled territory. Paragraph 3 specifically directs that the units place captured and disarmed Muslims in suitable premises where they can be guarded by small forces, and that this is to be reported immediately to the superior command. Moving to page 2 of this document, it discusses that on paragraph 6, "Ensure through the competent organs of the authorities that all the available manpower is engaged and that there is coordination in carrying out the above aforementioned tasks." Paragraph 7 directs that "Reports on captured and blocked groups --" or "report on captured and blocked groups on secure lines of communication." Again, we're talking here about the reporting of prisoners in this particular and that it should not be discussed openly. "Vigorously prevent all unnecessary and excessive conversations which may lead to a leaking of confidential conversation and indicate to the enemy our intentions and activities." And of course paragraph 8, "Through interim reports, provide an overview of the actual situation in all unit zones of responsibility in order to enable the Main Staff to take measures in good time." And this document is type signed by Lieutenant General Milan Gvero who is, of course, the assistant commander for morale, legal and religious affairs of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This document was not directed to the Bratunac Brigade. What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it's not directed to the Bratunac Brigade specifically, it is not an order that is directly applicable to them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Is that how you view it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's see what the next exhibit is.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This exhibit, Prosecution 467, is Drina Corps order 13 July 1995, which is in effect their amplification of the Main Staff order that we've previously discussed. You will note in this particular order it is directed to all Drina Corps subordinate units now inclusive of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade, and for the attention of the Drina Corps IKM 1 forward command post. In the first paragraph, it references the Main Staff order which we've previously discussed. And it is on this basis that I can conclude that this initial order was, in fact, a 13 July order from the Main Staff and its number was 03/4-1629. If you look at the actual text of the order itself, with very slight modifications, it reads as almost a direct lift from the Main Staff order. And as I had indicated in my earlier testimony, that is a relatively common practice within the VRS, on the transmission of orders from higher to lower. In paragraph 1 in this particular instance it specifically notes that brigade commands in their areas of responsibility will employ all available able-bodied men to discover, block, disarm, and capture any Muslim groups observed and prevent their crossing into Muslim territory. It also discusses the setting of around-the-clock ambushes along the entire Zvornik, Crni Vrh, Sekovici, Vlasenica road. Paragraph 3 indicates that they should put captured and disarmed Muslims in suitable buildings that can be secured by small forces and immediately inform the superior command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, are you aware of Muslim prisoners being put in buildings on the 13th of July in the Bratunac Brigade zone?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Notwithstanding the prisoners that were placed in the Kravica warehouse, you had additional groups of prisoners that were in a facility known as the hangar. You had groups of prisoners in a facility known as the Vuk Karadzic school. Very rapidly as those facilities filled to capacity, you had situations where the Bosnian Muslim prisoners were kept inside trucks or buses that were grouped together in other locations in and around the Bratunac area, which would include a grouping of buses and trucks in the village of Kravica. It would include a grouping of buses and trucks in the parking lot of the Vuk Karadzic school. It would also include groupings of buses and trucks at the Vihor transportation facility. As you can go through the rest of the paragraphs, again it is a direct lift from the Main Staff order, particularly with respect to paragraph 7. And this order, again noting that interim reports are required so that the command of the Drina Corps may be able to take measures in good time. So from a perspective of the brigade commands, the superior command in this case is the headquarters of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in your opinion would this order be directed to Mr. Blagojevic as commander of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, it would.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's go to the next exhibit. I believe it's 468. Can you tell us what this is.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This particular order, and as I've discussed earlier in my testimony, at a meeting that took place at the evening of 12 July 1995, it was determined that the army taking advantage of the current military and political situation in Eastern Bosnia at the time was going to reorient their mobile forces and attempt to capture the Zepa safe area. This order dated July 1995, in fact, is the operations order for the Zepa operation, which is known as Stupcana 95.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is the Bratunac Brigade's responsibility for this?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you go to page 3 of this particular order, paragraph 5/7, it notes that the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade presently is allotted a rather small part, that they are to allocate one company to join the Milici Light Infantry Brigade and carry out tasks assigned to that brigade. It notes that the company is to report to the commander of the Milici Light Infantry Brigade in the area of Bracan by 1800 hours on 13 July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And will we see this implemented in future exhibits?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, we will.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And whose name is this order made under?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This order is signed under the name of General Major Radislav Krstic as the chief of staff, and it will perhaps be more clear on the B/C/S version of the original.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you get an indication of any time associated with this order?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no obvious date, time stamp on the order, however, it is my understanding that certainly the drafting of this order would have occurred before General Krstic's assumption of command between 1800 and 2000 hours on 13 July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why do you think he's not in command at this time of the actual Drina Corps I should say, to be specific?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this particular time, although it's rather close, General Zivanovic is still the corps commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, what's the title that he drafts this document under?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Nacelnik Staba," is in fact chief of staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And let's go to the next document, Exhibit 469, I believe.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is the daily combat report of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade for 13 July 1995 to the command of the Drina Corps. Paragraph 1 discusses the enemy situation and the fact that their forces are not meeting resistance. It also reflects the fact that the command of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade is aware of a large enemy group that has been successfully encircled in the area of Konjevic Polje, Kasaba, and Pobudje. Paragraph 2 reflects what the assignments of the brigade are. I would direct your attention to the last sentence of paragraph 2 which indicates that the brigade command is working on the formation of a company to be sent to the area of Podravanje, the school, to carry out the assignment. Podravanje is located in the Bacan area and, in fact, this is an indication that the brigade is working on the task that has been assigned to it under the Stupcana 95 order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, yesterday you spoke briefly about Mr. Vasic's document where he said on the 13th he was working alone dealing with the Muslim column along the Konjevic Polje/Bratunac road. Does this document give us an idea where the Bratunac Brigade forces were on the 13th at that time?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, it does.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you just use the map again and tell us what it says and what you believe that means.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Ravni Buljim area is this general area in this location to the south of Kravica. And as indicated in paragraph 2, the troops are, at least at this point, beginning a limited movement out of their previously held line of defence and are pushing forward against the remnants of the Bosnian Muslim column.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as they push forward, the direction of the remnants of the Muslims would go where?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The column is continuing to move towards the crossing points between Konjevic Polje and Nova Kasaba. So it's becoming clustered in this area, and in fact this is the larger region that is discussed in the Bratunac Brigade report for paragraph 1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And can you tell us anything about the signatures or -- on this -- or drafts on this report, if we could go into the B/C/S version of this.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the handwritten version of the B/C/S draft of this -- my apologies -- this again reflects a signature which I've come to recognise as that of Colonel Blagojevic's.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's go on to the next exhibit. And just -- I'm sorry, before we leave that, can you give us any time estimate related to this document?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. If you go to the typed version or teletyped version, it reflects the communications clerk processing this document at 1545 hours on 13 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could go on to the next exhibit, 470.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an interim combat report from the command of the 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade to the command of the Drina Corps, reflecting that at 1700 hours "We sent a unit consisting of 92 soldiers led by the chief of staff to carry out the following tasks in the area of Bracan. The unit was sent in the direction of Bratunac, Milici, Bracan."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, can you show us what route -- just tell us what route they should have taken if they went in that direction, what roads they should have gone on.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not sure you need to stand up, but if you could just explain it.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Bratunac -- I'm going to have to stand. They would have travelled the road Bratunac, Konjevic Polje, Milici, and Bracan is approximately in this area right here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's due west a few kilometres from Zeleni Jadar on the map.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of any particular units that were assigned as part of this group of 92 soldiers?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this point in time, I'm not specifically aware of exactly which group of soldiers is going at this particular time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Any indication that the Red Berets were part of this unit?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are some indications that elements of the Red Berets were part of this unit, and we will get more visibility on the Red Berets in a future combat report which discusses their exact location.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What indication do you have that they may have been part of this unit?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: On 14 July there will be a Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade report indicating that the Red Berets are deployed with the Milici Brigade. And there will be further references to them with the Milici unit in intercepts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next document.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: One issue, if we could remain on this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: One thing of significance that I believe should be noted out with respect to the command process is that by sending the brigade chief of staff to carry out this mission personally, it leaves the commander as the focal point for information now within the entire brigade. He has, in effect, sent his deputy out of zone on a mission. And I just have to note in respect to the issue of command, that by doing that, he then becomes the sole focal point of any information that should be passed back and forth within the brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you, in relation to that, give the Trial Chamber a basic definition of the chief of staff duties in a brigade.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: With respect to a chief of staff, as we've noted, he also performs duties as the deputy commander, but he is the individual who is responsible for organising and coordinating the activities of the brigade staff. So he as an individual is the facilitator by which the brigade commander gives instructions and by which they are carried out in the process of orders to subordinates.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in the absence of the chief of staff, who takes over those duties?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be the chief of operations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know in the Bratunac Brigade who that might have been?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: My understanding of the individuals of the Bratunac Brigade at the time, I do not know who the designated operations officer was. The only officer that I'm able to identify based on my documents who was performing duties in July of 1995 during this period would be a Lieutenant Micic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And given the handwritten versions of this document, do you recognise any of the -- any handwriting or anything like that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. As you can see, there is no signature over the handwritten signature block.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Thank you. Let's go on to the next document, 471. And tell us what this is.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is the 13 July 1995 regular or daily combat report from the Drina Corps command to the Main Staff of the army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was this obtained from? Where did the OTP get this?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document was obtained from Colonel Obrenovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you have just recently been able to review this document?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what do you find significant in it for your narrative?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: With respect to paragraph 2, combat readiness, it reflects what the corps' missions are at that time. Specifically it notes the 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade and the 1st Milici Light Infantry Brigade are combing the terrain of the Srebrenica enclave. It reflects that the other groups or other combat groups from other corps units are carrying out the final preparations or last preparations for resolving the issue of the Zepa enclave. In paragraph 3, situation in the zone of responsibility, it notes that so far the transportation of 15.000 Muslims from Potocari to Kladanj has been organised. It also notes in the next paragraph under 3 that the corps command is aware that in Konjevic Polje and also in Nova Kasaba reception of Muslim civilians and soldiers who surrendered is being taken in an organised fashion. The second page reflects more general information as to logistical support, fuel, and ammunition usage. The third page reflects losses. It discusses the conclusions and projections for further action in paragraph 8. And as the final paragraph of paragraph 8, it notes what the commander's decisions are with respect to this. Particularly with respect to the second paragraph, it notes that part of the forces in coordination with MUP forces shall control the territory behind the lines, detect, block, capture, and disarm dispersed Muslim forces, protect the population and property, and at the same time secure the lines of defence from attacks from behind. It further notes that part of the forces in coordination with the MUP forces will control and set up ambush operations along the Muslim groups' axis of withdrawal, completely secure the Bratunac, Konjevic Polje, Milici, Vlasenica, and the Zvornik, Sekovici, Vlasenica roads, and make them passable around the clock.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the work of the part of the Drina Corps forces with the MUP in this area, how does that fit into your previous analysis on that similar subject?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe this in fact dovetails with my previous analysis that the forces of the Drina Corps brigades and the forces of the deployed MUP forces are operating under the command of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And who and what position has apparently written this order, or at least authored it.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This order is signed by Major General Radislav Krstic as the commander of the Drina Corps. And if you will go just below that, you will note an incoming received time stamp from the communications office of the Drina Corps reflecting that this document was received by them at 13 July at 1945 hours, was processed and sent by 2010 hours. And if I can take you to the last page of the B/C/S version of the order, this is in fact what it looks like.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in your opinion, who was commander of the Drina Corps at this time?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Major Radislav Krstic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And let's go to the next document, if you don't have anything else to say about that. This is 472. Now, just briefly, this appears to be another order by General Krstic as the commander at -- on 13 July. Can you tell in terms of time frame how it relates to the previous -- the daily combat report to the Main Staff that he signed.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The English language translation of the communications centre stamp, again reflects it arriving at the communications centre at 13 July 2000 hours and being processed through at 13 July 2030 hours. And if I can move to the B/C/S version of that, which unfortunately is not as readable as it should be, these are the markings on that. And again, the signature of General Major Radislav Krstic as the commander. This document specifically is an order to the commands of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade, the 1st Milici Light Infantry Brigade, and Skelani Separate Battalion with respect to carrying out sweep operations throughout -- and search operations through the liberated area of the former Srebrenica enclave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've interchanged the word "search" and "sweep." I know that the translations may be different, but when it says, "Search the terrain," what do you think is meant by that in this context of this order?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this context, I don't believe it is a simple reconnaissance. I believe the context is a sweep operation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And will we see more on this order later?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, we will.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you just briefly describe what that will be.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the next series of -- or in the next couple of exhibits, there will be a corresponding order from the commander of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade, which implements the tasks outlined in paragraph 1 of this order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And let's go to the next exhibit, which I believe is an evening intercept of 13 July, 1945 hours.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us about this.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Prosecution Exhibit 217. And it is a subscriber calling from General Krstic's location, which, on the basis of the previous documents will be the headquarters of the Drina Corps in Vlasenica, looking for a Ljubisa who has gone to Bratunac. It discusses a bus from Janja and it discusses ones arriving from Doboj. And based on those references which are locations where there are detachments of the Republika Srpska special police brigade, I believe this document reflects a conversation or somebody is looking for Mr. Ljubisa Borovcanin, who is the deputy commander of the special police brigade, and who is in fact in the Bratunac area, as we discussed earlier, particularly in and around the town of Bratunac at this time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just the basic subject matter of this is what, again, just to be clear?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well correspondent X is looking for an update on the status of the arrival of special police units, and specifically reflects that Ljubisa should call me at General Krstic's.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it's about reinforcements?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the context of that time, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's go to the next document, another intercept a little later, 2040 hours on the 13th, Exhibit 220.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is at 2040 hours. And it reflects a conversation between General Krstic and Ljubisa Borovcanin. Borovcanin notes where his location is at the time. When asked whether it is, he knows that he is here at the command post. I believe that the command post he is referring to is in fact the headquarters of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why is that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Given the general body of traffic that has been passed back and forth and that these are intercepts from the military communications network, indicates that if he's being intercepted in this conversation, he's talking over that network, and that would of course be the command post of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just the subject matter of this conversation, what do you think is going on here?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this particular respect, this is police Lieutenant Colonel Borovcanin updating General Krstic as to the situation with his units, and also asking whether there is anything special for us from you, at which point Krstic then replies he's working on that part. So this in context is a piece of information that I believe continues to confirm the relationship between the MUP, certainly special police brigade, and the army that the army is commanding the MUP operations at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at 2040 hours on 13 July, would that have been anywhere near the time of the Kravica warehouse killings?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This conversation would be occurring approximately three hours, three and a half hours from the beginning of the executions. And if survivor accounts are accurate, approximately an hour after the last of the series of shootings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And from your understanding, were Borovcanin's people involved in this?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: My understanding of the evidence base that we have is that the soldiers or the police of the 2nd Sekovici Detachment were principle players in this execution.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's keep going on to the next document, Exhibit 221, another intercept a little later in the evening, 2100 hours.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This particular conversation between Krsmanovic, who we've previously identified as the chief of transportation of the Drina Corps, and a correspondent Viskovic, whom I do not know his affiliation. The text of the intercept discusses the fact that at 2100 hours, there are 700 people in Sandici village. These individuals are Bosnian Muslims. It notes that buses need to stop there and load 10 pieces and bring them here to me. I'm not sure what that particular phrase means in context. On the broader level, it discusses the fact that there is still a process ongoing where Bosnian Muslim prisoners are being collected from these known collection points along the road and put in buses and trucks. And as the information before the Court indicates, at this late hour, many of the people who are picked up here will spend the evening of 13 July in those same buses and trucks at various locations in and around the Bratunac area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this comment as we go down a little farther, "You go there. Anyway, that's a Bratunac checkpoint. Have that loaded and brought here because I don't have any communication with the checkpoint from here." Can you make anything of what that means, that's a Bratunac checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this respect, I believe what they're discussing is a checkpoint that was set up by the Bratunac municipal police along the road from Bratunac to the Konjevic Polje intersection. I believe it was set up before the Kravica in order to prevent civilian traffic from going along that road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next series of documents. Well, 476 is the first one.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The next series of exhibits are English language translations of handwritten interrogation notes of Bosnian Muslim prisoners whom, as you read the context of the conversation you're able to determine or at least I'm able to determine that these people were taken prisoner during the day of 13 July 1995. These interrogation notes were found in the security office of the Bratunac -- or of the former Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade during the OTP search. Without going into many of the details of the information that's derived, I would again illustrate a point that I made earlier in my testimony about the identity of the prisoner. And that in each and every instance here, the first information that is obtained from the individual is his own personal identification to include his full name, date of birth, and where possible, place of birth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if you recall, do any of these individuals that you'll be briefly discussing come from Potocari, from the crowd at Potocari?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. These individuals, based on their stories, are individuals who were captured or surrendered from the Bosnian Muslim column on or about 13 July 1995. Let me be clear on that, on 13 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, this first person Resid Sinanovic, can you give us -- we've heard his name before, in what context?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that there is testimony before this Trial Chamber which identifies this individual as having been captured at Konjevic Polje on 13 July 1995 and taken from the location at Konjevic Polje towards the Bratunac Brigade headquarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And this individual and some of the others, did you research their name in the various missing lists?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the case of all of the individuals who we have records on as being interrogated, I attempted to match their names to the names of individuals who are on the ICRC missing list for Srebrenica 1995. As I've indicated in my narrative, all of the individuals who are interviewed as part of this interrogation are, in fact, on the ICRC missing list.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that include Resid Sinanovic?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I notice I'm a little over. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll resume at quarter to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, I think we finished with Mr. Sinanovic. And could you briefly put up the next group just to confirm. Now, Nazif Avdic. It says he was not a soldier, so is it possible he comes from Potocari?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. I believe he was part of the column.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The rest of these, are there references that would lead you to indicate that, Mr. Dedic, Mr. Husic, Mr. -- the other ones?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I think the information taken from them indicates that they're all from the column. And this is Prosecution Exhibit 477.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's then go to 478. Why is this different -- or do you know why this was broken down, these handwritten notes, in different exhibits like this? Or are they part of the same bunch, as far as you?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are part of the same bunch but this is just a separate note, as you can see on the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And Hasib Ibisevic is on the missing list?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: And just finishing with these three, just to point out that it is an indication of some individual taking the effort to interview these people and extract combat-related information for them that would certainly be useful for the various commanders who were planning operations against the column, hence the references to numbers and destination of the column.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And then 479, Mr. Husic is also missing -- from the ICRC missing list.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that -- can you tell the Court how people are identified in Bosnia regarding their names and -- so how you can gauge -- I know there may be another witness that talks about this subject of populations and the ICRC missing list, but how is it that you can compare names like this to a list with any sort of accuracy?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Given the general trend that there are many individuals who share the first and last name, and in many cases sometimes even the date of birth throughout the country, one of the key identifying features that is used by the residents of the country themselves, is part of the naming process to identify the individual as the son or daughter of -- and list the parents. That's a customary feature that we see. So when we -- or at least certainly when I and I know other researchers as well, when they cross index the names, it is not considered to be a conclusive identification until you get not only the family name and the first name, but also the parents' names as a match.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next exhibit, Exhibit 480. We're still on 13 July dealing with some command-type documents.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a document from the IKM of the Drina Corps, and if I could just note on the original B/C/S teletype version, in fact it says IKM Drina Corps Bratunac. And to point out the disparity on that, the handwritten version up here reflects part of that and we're missing, I think, one page of the handwritten version. I'll have to check. But again, the teletype version identifying the IKM is still in Bratunac at this particular junction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the English version just missed that, it looks like?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It missed the phrase Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So we should write that in on your English version. All right and tell us about this document, how it fits in.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is directed to the command of the Drina Corps intelligence department, and as you'll note from the signature, it's from Colonel Radoslav Jankovic who we've previously identified as a member of the Main Staff intelligence department.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you mean signature or signature block?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the signature block and if we go to the handwritten version of this, I believe that these have been identified as his initials.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This report informs the recipients that on 13 July 1995 at 2000 hours, the evacuation of the entire Muslim population was completed. It also notes the status of 57 wounded from the UNPROFOR base at the hospital of Bratunac -- I'm sorry there are noted 57 wounded are placed in the hospital at Bratunac. 18 more are transferred later and that there are 54 more wounded at the UNPROFOR base. It discusses tomorrow the efforts that will be organised pursuant to the evacuation of the 54 wounded from the UNPROFOR base. And in this respect, the deputy command of the battalion that we're referring to is not the deputy commander of the Bratunac Brigade or any of the VRS units. It is, in fact, Major Franken of the United Nations Dutch Battalion. It notes in the last paragraph or in the last paragraph of the section that the MUP are stealing on a massive scale from the UNPROFOR, noting they openly stole a Puch armour vehicle. They wanted to participate in the search of the UN base after the departure of refugees and reflecting that Colonel Jankovic categorically refused that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that tell us anything?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again it dovetails with my earlier analysis that the MUP is under army control during this period. The last paragraph noted as PS, postscript, reflects that, "I think that if we want to take over the enclaves of Zepa and Gorazde in the same way, it will be necessary to present the operation in Srebrenica in the media so as to show that we rendered adequate treatment to the civilians and even to soldiers who surrendered their weapons."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What significance do you give that comment?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Given the greater context of the situation, the only people who were being accorded that type of treatment are those people who are at the Bratunac medical centre and under the direct supervision of the UNPROFOR and other international agencies. That is not the general sense of the situation, particularly at this time, that is occurring everywhere else with respect to Bosnian Muslim prisoners of war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. If we could go to the next exhibit, I believe it is 481.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll try and keep this in somewhat of a temporal order. I did want to bounce back just to the issue, because it is at this time roughly when General Krstic is assuming command of the Drina Corps. And bringing the Court's attention to this particular document, which in fact reflects that act occurring.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did the OTP get this document from?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document was provided to the OTP during an interview with General Zivanovic who was the former commander of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And does the OTP have this document in what appears to be original inked format?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, it does.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I should say the other document of the 13 July Drina Corps daily combat report to the Main Staff provided by Mr. Obrenovic, does that document appear to be in the original inked form?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, it does. The issue of note here is that this is sent to all the subordinate formations of the Drina Corps, with the communications processing stamp of again 2000 hours, 13 July. And certainly the notification of subordinate formations of a change of command is a consistent act within the military chain of command. Everybody has to know who the commander is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. On that same subject, I think is the next exhibit, 482. I believe we are starting to get into the 14th of July. And I think the Court has heard quite a bit about what's going on on these days, so unless it's specific to a document, I don't think we need to go over that.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: With respect to 482, I'd like to point out to the Court that while it is dated 17 July and in fact you see that in the teletype version, and I'll point that out here, the document as written is, in fact, written on 14 July. And as you can tell from the communications clerk's notation, it was sent on 14 July. So I believe what you're looking at in that respect is a simple typing error on the part of the communications clerk.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So what is this?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It reflects another Drina Corps document, and it's simply noting that the Bratunac Brigade command is going to secure the presence of brigade members and members of the municipality authorities for the official farewell of General Zivanovic who had been the prior corps commander and that this function was supposed to take place at 1300 on 23 June. And in this respect when you go back to the written one, it does also, in fact, say 23 June. So I suspect the drafter of this particular message just missed that date. And in fact what we are talking about is an official function of 23 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the actual word that was used in your paraphrase was not what is actually here. This word is "hitherto." What is your understanding of that British word?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: As an American I'm not sure I should be commenting on British definitions. My understanding of the word "hitherto" is that it means up until then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. The next document.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Going back to the -- and referencing the 13 July 1995 order by General Krstic to the Bratunac Brigade to sweep the terrain, on the 14th of July, and this is Exhibit 483, the Bratunac Brigade publishes their order 453-2, which is in fact that ground search order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you very briefly just point out the general area that is being required to be swept by this order.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 1 Battalion, which is located between the Bratunac and Glogova area, from their defensive positions are being required to sweep in the generally southern direction. The 2nd Battalion from its positions are being -- to sweep in a south and westerly direction. The 3rd Battalion in a westerly direction to the former enclave. And the 4th Battalion, which has defensive lines off the road between Glogova and Kravica, is essentially being directed to first south and then hooked towards the west and to move up as far as the village of -- or the area of Sandici, in this area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And we'll be hearing more about this order in the various daily combat reports to come. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, we will.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Anything else that you wanted to comment on that order?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Broadly speaking, this is an excellent example of a commander exercising command, designating lines, designating where command posts will be. And this is completely consistent with the rules and regulations of the former JNA that were applicable at the time we've discussed prior. I would like to point out again on the original B/C/S version of this document, it is, in fact, signed by or has the signature of what I've come to recognise as that of Colonel Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do we have that original document in the evidence locker?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, we do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you had a chance to review that original?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I've seen all of the originals.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, can you tell from that document -- or can we can infer anything about where Mr. Blagojevic might have been when he signed it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I presume that the physical signing of this document would have occurred at the headquarters of the 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why is that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would have been the most logical place for him and his staff or the remaining staff at the time to process the order, come up with the specific task for the units, publish the order, and send it out to subordinate battalions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would that have been the same for one of the previous documents dated 13 July?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it have been also possible that he was in some other location and the document was couriered to him too. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is a possibility also, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next exhibit unless there's something else you wanted to say.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. Turning to Prosecution Exhibit 484, with respect to other activities of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade, the operations listed in the prior exhibit were not the only things that the brigade command was engaged in that day. This particular document urgent to the Drina Corps is a request for the relief of a unit of the Bratunac Brigade that is currently attached to the 4th Drina Light Infantry Brigade. And as I discussed previously in my testimony, the 4th Drina Light Infantry Brigade was deployed on the battlefield at Trnovo. This particular request indicates that the brigade still has prior orders to relieve a unit by 20 July 1995, and they're inquiring to the corps whether or not that plan is still in effect. And they wish to be informed by 15 July if they still have to carry out the orders to relieve that unit. Again, in this particular case the document is personally signed -- or again has the signature of what I believe to be Colonel Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, this doesn't really appear to involve much in the way of the specific issues of this case. Why have you chosen this particular document to discuss?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: These documents are consistent with the efficient and diligent exercise of command and are illustrative of that, demonstrating that despite the combat operations that are occurring, that the brigade command and staff is continuing to function along the lines that would be expected of a brigade command and staff under the circumstances.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And is that important in determining whether communications are open and functioning?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I believe that it indicates that they are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. What's the next document?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is Prosecution Exhibit 485, and it is the daily combat report to the command of the Drina Corps, dated 14 July 1995. Paragraph 1, it reflects the enemy situation, reflecting that their forces have not come across any forces as part of the operation. And notes that a small part of the enemy forces are still surrounded in the area of Bokcin Potok, Siljkovici and Mratinjci. Paragraph 2, it informs the Drina Corps that pursuant to their order their forces are participating in the encirclement of the enemy forces listed in point 1. It reflects that the brigade's pioneer platoon, and in this context pioneer is combat engineers, are de-mining the known mine fields along their defensive lines or their last defensive lines, and further reflects that the Red Beret platoon was sent at 1000 hours to the area of Milici to join the task in the direction of Zepa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so that would have been 1000 hours on the 14th of July that they were sent in that direction?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was the same direction that we saw the day before that the chief of staff took a group towards Zepa also. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure I could make that conclusion. Presumably by the 14th of July, the route from Bratunac through Srebrenica may very well have been open. However, the quickest route to Milici would have from Bratunac, Konjevic Polje, to Milici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, just the first paragraph, the area of Bokcin Potok that it describes where the enemy forces are, can you just tell the Court roughly where that is.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That area is to the south of the main -- of the highway, sort of in the triangle between Konjevic Polje, Nova Kasaba, and Sandici, in that series of terrained features there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to the next exhibit, which I think is -- takes us back to an exhibit that we've been to before. Is that right? We marked this as 456.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the base exhibit, if that is the base exhibit number, this is 486 which is an extract from the main Bratunac military police log. I'm not sure what the original exhibit number is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You're right. I need to hold this closer to my eyes.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: But this is an extract from the Bratunac Brigade military police log indicating the activities from the 14th to the 15th of July, 1995. It notes that the police were engaged in the escort of Muslim refugees. And at this particular time, particularly referring back to the document from Colonel Jankovic, the Bosnian Muslim women and children and elderly from Potocari, their evacuation had been completed by 2000 hours on 13 July 1995. So in context, the only activity that this can be will be escorting buses and trucks of Bosnian Muslim men from Bratunac to designated areas wherein the Zvornik Brigade's area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of testimony in this case that corroborated that fact?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't have that corroboration when you testified on this same point at the Krstic trial?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's go to the next exhibit.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's Prosecution Exhibit 487.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What organisation is this?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is going back to the series of reports from the Republika Srpska RDB or state security department. And I just raise it as an issue of the general awareness of the situation in the Bratunac municipality, which reflects that the state security people are aware that over that night a large Muslim group, their number is 5.000 of whom 500 are armed, which is present in the general area of Pobudje, Bratunac municipality, is allegedly planning a breakthrough of the Milici/Konjevic Polje/Drinjaca road in an attempt to advance towards Tuzla. It reflects the fact that to their knowledge, there are cases of Bosnian Muslim soldiers killing other Bosnian Muslim soldiers. And the last paragraph notes that the reports were submitted to the Zvornik SJB, the PJB special police unit, and the deputy commander of the RS MUP special brigade in the field, indicating that the information they are learning is, in fact, being passed to the 1st PJP company and the deputy commander who we know is Lieutenant Colonel Ljubisa Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you think as you're able to consider this many years after the fact and after much study of this figure of 5.000 Muslims?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suspect that given the time the figure of 5.000 is certainly inflated. There really is no way of knowing, other than the fact of trying to calculate how many people came out of the column when it crossed through the lines of the 17th and 18th -- or from the 16th to the 18th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you ever get any rough figure for how many of the Muslim column actually made it through to Nezuk on those days?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe the figures that I understand that are bandied around are approximately somewhere between 7.000 and 10.000 Bosnian Muslims made it out through the column.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Has that ever been determined to be a reliable figure because you say bandied about?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure that even after all of these years that the Bosnian Muslim government or now the Federation government has ever put that number together. There are still to this day, my understanding, various efforts to obtain surface remains of people who may be perished on the route of the column and things of that nature. I just don't know that that figure has ever been put out reliably.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's go to the next exhibit then. It's 488.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the Drina Corps daily combat report for 14th July 1995. Very quickly, paragraph 1, reflecting the enemy situation as they understand it. Paragraph 2, the second paragraph in heading 2 actually under combat readiness, reflects the corps command's knowledge that the terrain is being combed or swept by the 1st Milici Light Infantry Brigade, 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade, and the Skelani Separate Battalion, and that a large number of Muslims fleeing from the Srebrenica enclave have been surrendering. It notes in paragraph 7 under losses, two soldiers missing. I believe these individuals are from the Milici Light Infantry Brigade. And under paragraph 8, reflecting the conclusions and the decisions of the corps commander. And in most cases, they reflect the same conclusions and decisions that were listed on the 13th July report, so I don't need to read them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And paragraph 2 relating to the Bratunac Brigade. What's -- concentrating on the Bratunac Brigade, of course, what's their understanding of what they're doing?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Their understanding at the corps level is that the Bratunac Brigade is implementing the order that was given to them by the Drina Corps on the 13th of July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now I believe we're going to get into the 15th of July, and particular intercepts involving Mr. Beara. If we could go to the first one, 243, 15 July at 0952 hours.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This particular extract is -- or synopsis from which we have out of one of the Bosnian Muslim intercept books is the first of a series of three series of communications involving Colonel Beara, General Zivanovic, and General Krstic, that discusses specifically issues relating to prisoners of war and their execution. What I'd like to highlight in this and as I've referenced in my narrative, at this point in time, I believe that Colonel Beara is located at the headquarters of the Zvornik Infantry Brigade. The instruction that he needs to be called or that he wants General Zivanovic to call him at extension 139, that extension corresponds to the phone number of the security officer of the Zvornik Infantry Brigade, Lieutenant Drago Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that topic, before we go into the next one, can you track for us your knowledge about the whereabouts of Colonel Beara before this. I mean, if this puts -- this speaks for itself. But before that, where do you think he was and why?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In a series of intercepts that are later exhibits with respect to the Zvornik Brigade, what becomes clear is that on the 14th of July, Colonel Beara is in the Bratunac Brigade area. And specifically, during the evening of 14 July 1995, Colonel Beara is contacted at Badem, which is of course the headquarters of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And how about the 13th of July.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: As previous intercepts have indicated, Colonel Beara is in and around the Bratunac area and the Nova Kasaba area with respect to prisoners on 13 July 1995. And of course I understand that there has been testimony before this Trial Chamber also relating to the physical presence of Colonel Beara in and around the Bratunac Brigade area later that evening -- I'm sorry, the Bratunac area later that evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And we have -- you have -- well, we have organised some of these exhibits in the context of the Zvornik Brigade, that's why out of the chronological context. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it's fair to say you and I helped try to put this together in a chronological context and tried to make it make as much sense as possible?
