utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And let's go to the next exhibit.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Prosecution Exhibit P244. And this is a 15 July intercepted communication between General Zivanovic and Colonel Ljubo Beara.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before we get into this, are there, as the Court knows, various versions of these intercepts?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe in this instance, there are two versions of the intercept.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just why did you pick the particular one that you've chosen?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that the particular one that I've chosen is the most complete version. I understand as a part of the process that, depending on which site collected it, some parts of the conversation may have been omitted or some parts of the conversation may have been omitted by operator. So the versions that I am picking to display as exhibits are those versions which I believe are the most complete in context.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So tell us about this intercept, in particular the participants at the top?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, General Zivanovic, who we know was at the Drina Corps headquarters at Vlasenica on the morning of 15 July, even though he was no longer the commander. And of course the conversation, the other person is Colonel Beara.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know Zivanovic was at the Vlasenica headquarters?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The OTP has interviewed General Zivanovic and he has in fact confirmed being at the Vlasenica headquarters that morning. I would have to note, however, that when showed this conversation he had a somewhat different reaction at that point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Butler, have I instructed you to try to, unless specifically asked, to limit your answers regarding witnesses that have not testified on potentially important issues?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, you have. And I've tried to do so as much as possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Clearly you have had access to all the interviews of the various people in this case. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. What can you tell us about this conversation?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Without going through line by line, the context of this conversation is Colonel Beara talking to General Zivanovic and going through the problem that Colonel Beara is having that one of the subordinate commanders, Furtula, did not send Lukic's intervention platoon, as was instructed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Remind us who Furtula -- and who you think Furtula and Lukic are?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel Furtula, or at that time Major Furtula, was the commander of the 1st Rogatica Light Infantry -- I'm sorry, the 1st Visegrad Light Infantry Brigade. And Lukic, I believe, is a reference to Milan Lukic who is, in fact, a member of that unit in July 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And after that comment about Furtula and Lukic, Zivanovic says: "And Lukic is waiting at Blagojevic." And then Beara said: "Lukic is here with me and his driver and we urged that." So the question: "And Lukic is waiting at Blagojevic." What do you think that means?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That indicates that General Zivanovic had some prior knowledge of what the context of this conversation was and believed that in this particular instance Lukic would be going to the headquarters of the 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would that be Nedjo Blagojevic from the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the context of the events, I don't believe that it would be that individual.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But does Beara clear up the location situation in the next line?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, he does.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain that.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Beara indicates that Lukic is here with me as well as his driver, and that instead of sending a group of individuals, they only sent two soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where do you think Beara is at the time he's having this conversation with Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've indicate previously, I believe this conversation is occurring and Colonel Beara is at the headquarters of the Zvornik Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And let's just keep going down it.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Beara reflects that he, Furtula, in this instance doesn't give a damn about what the commander orders him to do and that he has a platoon of 60 men. And Beara is asking that have him at least send half that platoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who do you think Beara is referencing when he says "the commander"?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that Colonel Beara is referencing his commander, which would be General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. And then Beara -- Zivanovic says something that we can't hear and Beara says: "Have him send at least half." Zivanovic says: "Yes, yes." Beara says: "Say again?" Zivanovic says: "To send them immediately." Beara says: "Yes." Zivanovic says: "I can't arrange for that anymore." What do you make of "I can't arrange for that anymore"?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe in that same time that General Zivanovic is informing Colonel Beara that he is no longer in a position to give orders to brigade commanders of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then what happens in this conversation?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Beara notes that and Zivanovic says the number 385.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what the significance of 385 as we go down, it says Zlatar 385 and V. What do you think that means?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zlatar is the telephonic code name for the headquarters of the Drina Corps. And 385 is an extension that we come to associate with General Krstic, further brought down to the IKM, which is now in Krevic. So extension 385 is a line that runs to the Drina Corps IKM in Krevic controlling to Zepa operation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why do you think that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe a series of intercepts we have in the future, and I'm not sure that I have them as exhibits, but they're in context in my report, indicates that other subscribers in other intercepts will instruct people to call for General Krstic and they are instructed to call at the IKM, extension 385, and indicate that that's where General Krstic can be reached.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Before going on to the other conversation, what do you make of the fact that we have in this case what appears to be Main Staff chief of security Beara contacting General Zivanovic for troop resources?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: My interpretation of that conversation is that what you're seeing is reflective of the normal command and staff process. While Colonel Beara by, I believe everyone's account, is a major principal in the commission and controlling or should I say behind many of the executions and the greater organisation thereof, Colonel Beara does not control troops or resources. Those belong to the commanders. In this particular instance, Colonel Beara is complaining to General Zivanovic because a brigade commander, formerly his brigade commander, had not followed the order of the plan. And as a result, Colonel Beara's operations were impacted. Colonel Beara in and of himself does not have the authority to directly ring up the brigade commander and demand that troops be sent. He has to do this explicitly through that brigade commander superior officer who, in effect, is the corps commander. In this particular context, Colonel Beara, for whatever reason, obviously isn't aware that General Zivanovic is no longer authorised to give orders to his brigade commanders or that, in effect, General Zivanovic is no longer the Drina Corps commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, while we're on this subject, do you see anything similar to this, this relationship that you've talked about between a security officer and a commander occur in the next conversation, without getting into the detail of the conversation we'll do that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, it is consistent with the next conversation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you just set the scene for us. Why -- I don't want to get into the detail right now, but what -- who is that conversation between and how is it similar to what you've just talked about?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: What will happen is that in a few minutes, Colonel Beara, following General Zivanovic's instructions in this matter, calls and is connected -- and talks to the corps commander, General Krstic. In that particular series of discussions, Colonel Beara will relate the same problem, that one of now General Krstic's subordinates, Furtula, did not send the required assets. And that he is asking that General Krstic become involved and make available additional resources to solve Colonel Beara's problem. It is a reflection again of the fact that the security branch does not have the authority to directly contact and take assets away from either the corps or subordinate brigades, that these individuals and resources are under the command and direction of commanders who have to make them available themselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, again, just very briefly, fast forward to the situation that you know about now regarding a security officer for the Zvornik Brigade, Dragan Nikolic and his communication with his commander, Dragan Obrenovic.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe the context of that communication is, again, reflected in my analysis of those types of conversations. A security officer having to request from the commander that resources be made available for him to carry out his mission, that he does not have the independent authority to take from subordinate or to take from his own brigade command. So I believe that you have a consistent pattern of this at all levels, which indicates the practical functionality between the commands and their security officers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One more example, and I know we'll get into some more specifics a little later, but Lieutenant Colonel Popovic, the chief of security of the Drina Corps and his commander General Krstic, do you have any insight into their communications of the subject at hand?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In a series of future exhibits, one of the features that will -- or one of the circumstances that will occur during the date of 16 July 1995 is that Colonel Popovic will require additional fuel resources to complete the execution operations which are occurring at the Branjevo Military Farm. And in a series of intercepted communications between Palma, which is the Zvornik Brigade, and Zlatar, the headquarters of the Drina Corps in Vlasenica, you see the Zvornik Brigade relaying Colonel Popovic's request for fuel to the Drina Corps chief of technical services for approval. And of course that approval is being given and the Zvornik Brigade is authorised to disperse the fuel. It again demonstrates the limits of a security officer with respect to his ability to take resources from a particular brigade. In this case, Colonel Popovic of his own authority could not demand fuel from the Zvornik Brigade, it has to go through the proper chain for approval.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, briefly, on a related issue, do you see Colonel Popovic communicating with his commander, General Krstic, about this operation to kill and bury prisoners?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the later afternoon or early evening hours of 16 July, while we do not see a direct conversation between Colonel Popovic and the Drina Corps commander, what we will see is a conversation where Colonel Popovic is calling the Zlatar duty officer and basically requesting that the Zlatar duty officer inform the commander that the job has been completed. So in this instance you have the security officer making sure that his commander is informed about the events that are occurring.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So these communications that you've just made reference to that I've asked you about, is it important to understand those communications when looking at the communications or potential communications between Momir Nikolic and his commander?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I believe they are fundamental.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, with that background, let's go into this next conversation and whichever of the versions of it you've chosen to discuss. Just let us know the exhibit number. I know you have brought forward some of the other versions of it in case you're asked about that or need to mention it.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are a number of versions. I believe that the version I'm going to display is the one that I believe is listed in my narrative. I tried to be as consistent as possible in that respect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And just tell us --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I'm not, I'm sure you can bring that to my attention. I believe it is. Since there are four or five versions of this conversation in the form of exhibits, I want to try and make it as extremely clear as possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what exhibit number is this?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Prosecution Exhibit 245.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Excuse me, which 245?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: There's more than one 245 as I understand it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Going to the ERN number might be helpful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. McCloskey, maybe you could ask some questions to this witness asking him to identify which is which, because we see so many 245s, we don't see the /A, /B, /C, /D.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you and I think, as we've learned yesterday, it's a good idea to refer to the ERN number along with 245, since they all have those.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this particular instance, the document that we're referring to from the original notebook is ERN 00804535 and the English language translation is 009126 -- and I believe that is a 11. It may be a 14. I cannot tell. It's kind of unclear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll check that out. Okay. Now, can you relate again in -- I know I've diverted you slightly, but in terms of time, how long is this conversation after the one between Beara and Zivanovic, according to these -- this information?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Depending on which version or which site has collected it, one reflects the conversation occurring at 1000 hours, six minutes afterwards. And on another site collection, you will see a time pack that says 0955 which is less than 1 minute. So certainly no more than six minutes from the first conversation, Colonel Beara immediately gets in touch with General Krstic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Can you take us through this conversation and give us your analysis of its meaning.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this particular version, it reflects that Beara is discussing and informing General Krstic that Furtula did not carry out the boss's order. And again, I understand the boss being General Mladic in this particular instance. General Krstic replies, "Listen, he ordered him to lead out a tank, not a train." For me, this indicates that General Krstic had an awareness of what resources or how many people that Major Furtula was supposed to send up for this mission. And of course Beara in the next line says, I need 30 men, just like it was ordered. General Krstic then responds about taking them from Tasic or Sladojevic. In this particular instance, whom I believe he's referring to are the individuals Nastic and Blagojevic, and you will see them again further down. I believe the effect you're having here is the operators did not hear the names clearly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know of any Tasic?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not within the context of the command entities of the Drina Corps or subordinate brigades.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How about Sladojevic?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That name is associated with an officer of the Main Staff who we see on 17 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what kind of an officer is that? Would that be the kind of officer that had troops?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. He is an officer from the Main Staff operations section.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's keep going then.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: He notes that he can't pull anything out of here for you. And perhaps to understand this in context, on the morning of 15 July, as the gravity of the situation in the Zvornik Brigade zone has become clear to everybody in the Drina Corps, General Krstic has already at this point released the units of the Zvornik Brigade, which will be the Drina Wolves the two battle groups of the Zvornik Brigade including the Drina Wolves from the Zepa battlefront and has directed them to proceed to Zvornik as rapidly as possible to defend that area from the threat from the Bosnian Muslim column. So in this context he has already pulled two battle groups out of the Zepa operation and is clearly at the point where he is not willing to pull anything else out if he doesn't have to. Colonel Beara responds that he doesn't have anyone here. He needs them today and he is prepared to release them back to General Krstic tonight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We see this "Krle, you have to understand. I can't explain it to you." You've talked about Krle before?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I have. That is a nickname, of course, of General Krstic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does that indicate to you, if anything, that Colonel Beara can refer to a corps commander by his nickname?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It indicates a certain amount of familiarness. Moving down, General Krstic again indicates that he will be disturbing the -- everything on his axis, again his attack --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is this -- I'm sorry. What is this axis? What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In a military respect, an axis is a particular direction of attack. So in the greater context, General Krstic is talking about the ongoing military operations against Zepa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. The next line.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel Beara reiterates that he needs 15 to 30 men with Boban Indjic and he cannot do anything. Now, Boban Indjic is known to be a subordinate of Milan Lukic from the Visegrad Brigade. And as the Court may be aware, they have been -- both of those individuals are under indictment for events that occurred in the Visegrad area in 1992. Krstic or General Krstic at this time reminds Colonel Beara that this phone line is not secure, and Beara acknowledges that. In the next line, General Krstic again responds, "I will see what I can do, but it will disturb a lot." He then says: "Please, you have some men down there at Nastic's and Blagojevic's." In this context, he's referring to two of his subordinate brigade commanders, Major Nastic, the commander of the Milici Brigade, and Blagojevic, the commander of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade. Colonel Beara is saying: But I don't have any, and if I did -- or if I did, I wouldn't still be asking for the third day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what do you make of this "third day"? What does that -- what do you think that means?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Subtracting backwards in time, today being the 15th of July 1995, depending on whether you count this day as the beginning of the third or the day prior, what you have as an indication is that by the 12th or 13th July of 1995, everyone knew what the plan was going to be. And in this particular case with Colonel Beara, the plan is the elimination of the Bosnian Muslim prisoners of war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where do you get that from? How do you make that conclusion?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, everyone who we've talked to for the investigation, and even with respect to General Krstic himself as a component of his trial, have indicated that they all consider Colonel Beara to be one of the principal organisers of these mass executions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does the information in this intercept as we go down and other information, is it consistent with that conclusion?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let's go down --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mild objection. If we could just get to the information, the Trial Bench can reach that conclusion. It is leading in nature. I've been patient, I think. But I would prefer if we just go through the information and then the gentleman can be asked: What do you conclude from that? And he can give us a conclusion as opposed to forecasting a conclusion and then we hear it. That's all I'm asking. I know he's an expert but even experts should abide by the fundamentals.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey, if there is an objection from the Defence team, I believe you have to go slowly step by step.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. And as the Court knows, we're at day -- July 15 now, so this conclusion is well into the events. And I will -- it's my purpose and I think the Court and counsel probably see, I am not asking Mr. Butler to make the Court's conclusions. We are generally pointing out the facts, and some conclusions are inevitably made. But it is not my purpose to have Mr. Butler be the trier of this case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's -- after this comment about he's been asking -- still asking for the third day, what do you think he's been asking about for three days?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this particular instance, he's asking for resources necessary to commit the executions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then the next line, "Check with Blagojevic, take his Red Berets." Which Blagojevic do you think that is?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly the connection with Blagojevic and the Red Berets clearly identifies that individual as Colonel Blagojevic, the commander of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade. The Red Berets, again, being a formation subordinate to his 3rd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then Beara says: "They're not there. Only four of them are still there. They took off," expletive. "They're not there anymore." So what do you make of that sentence?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two issues on this particular sentence. One, clearly Colonel Beara already has an awareness that the Red Berets are not available. That would not be surprising, given his presence at the Bratunac Brigade headquarters the prior evening as the --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remind us of the Red Berets from the previous document.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. The Red Berets, as you're aware, were listed in the Bratunac Brigade daily combat report of 14 July, as going to the Milici area where they would subsequently become involved in military operations as Zepa. Krstic responds: "I'll see what I can do." Beara: "Check it out and have them go to Drago's." This is another indication in the greater context that the location of Colonel Beara and where he wants the reinforcements sent is Drago Nikolic of the Zvornik Infantry Brigade. Again, General Krstic indicating that he cannot guarantee anything and I'll take steps. Colonel Beara, apparently showing some form of exasperation, noting that "Krle, I don't know what to do anymore." General Krstic responds: "Ljubo, take those MUP guys from up there."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who do you think General Krstic means by the "MUP guys from up there"?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The "MUP guys from up there," in this context will be either one of two categories of police. They will either be the special police brigade under Borovcanin's people or they will be the PJP companies under Vasic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Beara's response: No, they won't do anything. I talked to them. So what does that mean?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is evident in that sentence that Colonel Beara has discussed that issue of obtaining resources from the MUP and that they have turned him down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the significance of that to you in this overall evaluation?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suspect that putting it in the greater context of the situation that's occurring, while the MUP understood themselves to be under army command for the combat operations that were occurring, the local MUP commanders on the ground or their superiors, be it Colonel Borovcanin or Dragomir Vasic, were not prepared to interpret that as also being under the army's command to commit mass executions. And Beara then further says: "There is no other solution but those 15 to 30 men with Indjic," again reflecting that they were supposed to arrive on the 13th but didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there another intercept that helps us with Mr. Indjic and his non-arrival on the 13th?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, and in one of the following exhibits there is an intercept that sheds some light as to why those individuals did not arrive on time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just briefly, what's that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Essentially their bus broke down and there was no replacement bus available to go get them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, do you want me to finish this conversation or this is also time to break in the conversation if you like.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, maybe you could finish this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Then it -- Krstic says: "Ljubo, you have to understand me, too. You guys have fucked me up so much." In the context of what General Krstic is doing, what do you think this means?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Given the context of the army now having to deal decisively with the Bosnian Muslim column and at the same time having to continue offensive operations with the goal of trying to eliminate the Zepa enclave, the issue now of executing the prisoners and the manpower involved behind that has now become a significant drain on the forces -- or on the ability of General Krstic to accomplish his mission. And that is what I believe he is complaining about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And the next line: "I understand, but you have to understand me, too. Had this been done then, we wouldn't be arguing over it now." What -- does that fit with what's been said?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that's consistent within the context of both parties understanding what was supposed to have been accomplished then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Then Krstic does an expletive. "Now I'll be the one to blame." What blame would there be in this situation?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are several ways to interpret this. Clearly as the commander, if something is not accomplished with respect to any one of the three things that are up in the air right now, one being the column, two being Zepa, and three being the executions, he feels that he'll be the one to blame if something goes wrong in any one of those.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then Beara says: "I don't know what to do. I mean it, Krle, there are still 3500 parcels that I have to distribute and I have no solution." This term "parcels" which I believe is the Bosnian word paket, what is your understanding of the meaning of what he's referring to here?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we see that phrase in the intercepts, that's generally the phrase that they will use for people. We see it in two contexts in the intercepts. With respect to reinforcements moving back and forth across the battlefield, they will refer to them as packages of 20 or 30 from a certain location. In this particular context, I believe what he is referring to is that he has 3500 prisoners. The phrase "distribute," the euphemism to kill, and he has no solution to that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Finally before we take our break, can you tell us at about 10.00 a.m., the time of this call on 15 July, what is the prisoner situation in terms of their location and their fate, and as rough as you can tell us, the numbers.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Generally speaking, given the situation of prisoners moving into the Zvornik Brigade on 13 and 14 July 1995, there are five locations -- or four locations -- five locations, I'm sorry, where we see them collected. As the sites fill up, the first one is Orahovac, the second one is Petkovci, the third one is the school at Rocevic, the fourth one is the school in Pilica, also known as the school in Kula. And the fifth one is the dome of culture in Pilica which begins to fill up once the school is full in Pilica. In time from when we know the executions occur, and we'll be able to go into that in detail in future exhibits, by the time this conversation takes place at 10.00 on 15 July, with the exception of the four survivors from Orahovac, the close to 800 to 1.000 prisoners who were at that facility are all dead and they are still being buried. By the morning of 15 July, the roughly 500 to 800 prisoners that were held in the new school at Petkovci are dead, with the exception of our two known survivors. There are still roughly 500 to 800 people, we estimate, at the school in Rocevic whose executions have not yet occurred. There is also roughly 1.000 people in the school at Pilica who we know will not get executed at the Branjevo Military Farm until the 16th and also approximately 300 to 500 people at the Pilica dome of culture. So roughly speaking at the time this conversation takes place, almost half of the prisoners in the Zvornik Brigade zone of responsibility are already dead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But there are still many, many survivors at this time, is that right, or many people that have not been killed?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Krstic appears to end the conversation with: "I'll see what I can do."

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This would be a good time to stop, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, yes. We'll resume at 20 to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, if we could go to the next exhibit, 216, it's an intercept from 13 July. Is this what you were referring to earlier about the problem with Boban Indjic?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you just briefly tell us about what you think is happening in this intercept.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It reflects the discussion between two unidentified subscribers, whether or not there is a bus available at that time. And the Y subscriber indicates that there is in fact one and that it needs to be sent down towards Visegrad, Podravanje and Rogatica, and further. And then when they come across a bus of soldiers, those are the ones from Visegrad, Boban is their commander, later it's Boban Indic, and X says they are then to bring them to the command in Bratunac. The rest of the conversation reflects that they need to send a bus and driver immediately and notes that their vehicle has broken down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So how do you fit that into the information where Mr. Beara is not very pleased with Boban Indjic's commander Furtula on the 15th of July?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Reading that in context with this intercept it is evident that at least for his part Major Furtula did, in fact, send some people and that the bus broke down and as a result they were not able to make it to where they were supposed to be at the designated time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And 13 July at 1919 hours, what was the situation with buses? And as I know, the Court probably already knows but ...

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this point in time, the last of the Bosnian Muslims would have been moved out of Potocari and buses and trucks were rapidly being filled up with Bosnian Muslim prisoners taken along the road. And as we have discussed as events will occur, because there was no room at the facilities in Bratunac, these prisoners spent the night on those vehicles at various locations in and around Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on the 14th, those buses and trucks were used for what?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Beginning with the first known movement of prisoners out of Bratunac at approximately 2000 hours on 13 July 1995, from that point to the 14th and even on some part of the morning of the 15th, those buses and trucks were used to move Bosnian Muslim prisoners from the Bratunac area into the zone of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, let's -- with that little background, let's now continue to the next exhibit which should be 489. It looks like another one of the CSB Zvornik from Mr. Vasic.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. This is his -- or a report on 15 July 1995. And in this report he discusses the situation in his zone, the police zone, and where all of the MUP forces are deployed. Paragraph 1 notes that the second company of the PJP forces is securing the town of Srebrenica and conducting police affairs. And just to note in that instance, in this context I would add that in Srebrenica in conducting police affairs, I do not consider that to mean that the second company is under any form of command of the armed forces. So when we talk about the police and MUP forces, at this time, the second company is excluded. They are conducting their normal Ministry of Interior related issued. Paragraph 2 reflects two companies of the MUP from Jahorina on the -- or in the road Kravica, Konjevic Polje, Kasaba. And I believe the Court is aware of the origin of those two companies and in this particular instance I note that they are under army control. It also reflects that one platoon from the PJP company from Zvornik, a tank and a crew, as well as elements of the police centre for dog breeding and training, are engaged with tasks to block the terrain and are engaged in combat with the remnants of the Muslim forces. Paragraph 3 starts to discuss the police dispositions around the town of Zvornik. And of course on 15 July, the situation was very tense in the Zvornik Brigade zone as the Bosnian Muslim column was at the point of now being able to engage in significant combat operations against the Zvornik Infantry Brigade. And the town of Zvornik was under a very real risk of being captured or invested by this column, had they chose to do so. So paragraph 3 reflects those dispositions and where police companies have been moved in from. Paragraph 4 notes that offensive forces of the MUP contained in parts of the second and fourth -- it says "SOP," that is the acronym or abbreviation for the special police brigades. As well as the special police brigade, the 2nd and 4th Detachments, as well as the 1st company of the PJP Zvornik, reinforced by the tank, Praga, a BOV, which are armoured fighting vehicles, and a mortar company or in this case it would just be a mortar section, are heading up in the direction of Crni Vrh, Bokrevica [phoen] to block the terrain together with the army and to destroy the forces trying to push out from Srebrenica. And I believe in the context of the testimony of Colonel Obrenovic, the Court is very familiar with the interrelationships in that part, so I don't need to get into those.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next exhibit for the 15th of July. It should be --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: P490, the 15th of July, the regular daily combat from the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This report is directed, of course, to the command of the Drina Corps. And rather uniquely, it is directed to the IKM of the Drina Corps in Krivaj. Not only are they ensuring that the headquarters of the Drina Corps in Vlasenica sees this report, but that it is being sent to the IKM, presumably for General Krstic. It notes that strong enemy forces in front of the forward positions of the 4th Battalion on the brigades right flank are carrying out combat activities and are regrouping in the direction of Konjevic Polje. Paragraph 2 reflects what their forces are doing, searching the terrain in accordance with the Drina Corps order from 13 July. The second part of paragraph 2 also reflects that part of our forces has been sent to the area of the Zvornik Light Infantry Brigade, in fact it is Infantry Brigade. It designates that it is 80 soldiers and an S-2M platoon has been sent to the 2nd Romanija Motorised Brigade area of responsibility. So during this period and while I do not have a specific order that designates it as such, clearly the commander of the Bratunac Brigade has been directed to send reinforcements to the zone of the Zvornik Brigade on the 15th of July. In fact, we know from other records that the unit that was sent is, in fact, the 4th Infantry company of the 2nd Infantry Battalion of the Bratunac Brigade. It notes the general situation in the territory, paragraph 3. And notes that a soldier from the 4th Battalion was wounded and later died as a result of combat activity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just regarding the signature of this document.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you look at the original in this particular case, you will note that it is not signed by the commander, but instead there is a "za" and a signature here. And I believe, as I previously indicated, that signature I recognise as that of being of Lieutenant Micic who is an operations officer in the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next document, I believe is 491.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. This is the 15 July 1995 regular combat report of the, Drina Corps to the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska. Again, it, details the enemy situation in the zone of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you just tell us about the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. With respect to the issues of Bratunac, in the third, paragraph of topic 1, it notes that the remains of dispersed Muslim formations from the former Srebrenica enclave are moving towards Kravica and Konjevic Polje with the objectives of, of course, crossing Mount Udrc towards Tuzla. Moving further down to combat readiness, in the second paragraph it reflects that the Milici Brigade, Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade, and Skelani Separate Battalion are combing the terrain with part of their forces in order to find these residual soldiers and groups. Situation in the zone of responsibility notes, again, that some of the roads are endangered by enemy groups. And one particular road Caparde Crni Vrh, Zvornik is already disconnected. It also notes a reference that we also saw in the Bratunac Brigade report that 51 UNPROFOR soldiers were moved to the FRY during to the day and those, or course, are members of the UNPROFOR that were in the custody of the VRS and had been taken into custody in the days proceeding the fall of the enclave. On the last page of the English language translation, also reflecting the death of a soldier from Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade, and the conclusions and projections for further activity. And if I can go to the original B/C/S version, the report is signed by Radislav Krstic as commander of the Drina Corps. And the date processing is roughly 15 July between 1915 and 1945 hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did this document come from?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document was provided by Colonel Obrenovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And have you seen what appears to be an original inked version of this?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next document, 492.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Following that daily combat report, the Drina Corps command also publishes an interim combat report, reflecting that due to the late report from the Zvornik Brigade, they're submitting additional information. With respect to this, the only issue that I think is relevant that I'd like to draw the Court's attention to is the last line of the third paragraph, noting that the brigade, meaning the Zvornik Brigade, shall forward details on enemy groups in a separate report about which you will be duly informed. That is significant in so much as we know that the interim combat report of 15 July from the Zvornik Brigade is the report by Colonel Vinko Pandurevic which discusses the issue of guarding the prisoners and the burial of bodies after their execution and reflects that his brigade can no longer handle that task and that he needs additional resources.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to be clear, that report, does it actually mention executions?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. It mentions the phrase "security obligations," which I take to be guarding the prisoners. And it mentions the phrase "asanacija," which I take to mean the burial of bodies afterwards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I think we'll get to that. And I think the Chamber has seen that previously, as well. So is this significant?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again this is signed by Radislav Krstic between 1945 and 2000 -- or 2010 hours is when it was processed. And in looking at this report, it is clear that the Drina Corps command in general and General Krstic in particular have some knowledge of what is occurring in the Zvornik Brigade and are alerting the Main Staff that they know that Colonel Pandurevic's interim report is coming and they will be forwarding it to the Main Staff as soon as they get it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that reference to guarding prisoners and asanacija in an official report unique to the various documents and materials you've seen?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is one of the few documents by which a commander in writing actually lays out the involvement of units under his command in unlawful activities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's go to the next exhibit, which I believe is 493. Can you briefly tell us what this is, why you've chosen it, what its significance is.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an order dated 15 July 1995 for the formation of a combat unit to be deployed to Trnovo. As I had testified and noted in an earlier exhibit, the Bratunac Brigade was requesting direction from the Drina Corps whether or not they would still have to send this unit. And while we do not have the response from the Drina Corps, I believe it's evident from this document that the answer was that they were expected to send a unit. And it reflects that on 15 July, the brigade command was active in that process of selecting the individuals who would be going as part of that unit. This particular document, if you go to the B/C/S version, is also signed by the signature of what I believe is Colonel Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you seen the original of this document?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next exhibit then. I believe it's P494, which is what we can now recognise as a page out of the military police log of the Bratunac Brigade. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What can you tell us about this?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Simply what it says, it's a reflection that the military police are working on the searching and combing of the area as well as apprehending getting Muslims found hiding in the area. A very nondescript and traditional mission for them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to find any documents or intercepts or reliable information regarding Muslim prisoners taken by the MPs on this date?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's go to the next exhibit, P495, and if you can just briefly tell us about this exhibit and how it's significant to your analysis.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Places this in time context of the events occurring, in the zone of the Drina Corps, what has been occurring through the day of the 15th is a situation where the forces of the Drina Corps are being stretched to the absolute limit with respect to the military and the unlawful execution operations which are occurring. In this particular report, the individual who is drafting it is Colonel Ignjat Milanovic, who you will remember was a figure in the 13 July intercepts looking for bulldozers and is, of course, a Drina Corps staff officer. He is the air defence chief of the Drina Corps. This is delivered to the command, directed to the forward command post, attention the commander, which would be Colonel Krstic, the Milici brigade and the Skelani Separate Battalion, and is noted in the header information it is being written from Bratunac. As part of the function of this report, he's laying out: In accordance with your instructions, and in this particular instance "your" is General Krstic, he travelled to Milici and Bratunac to acquaint himself with the situation to the east of the Milici/Konjevic Polje/Bratunac road. He discusses what the mission of the 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade is doing and he notes what the 1st Milici brigade is doing as well. He indicates orders that he has given on behalf of General Krstic and he's making General Krstic aware of what those orders are. Paragraph 4 specifically pertains to the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade. Then in this document he makes a series of proposals to the commander of the Drina Corps. And the first one is that the commander of the Drina Corps authorised and appointed the commander of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade as the commander of all forces participating in search operations in searching the terrain and sweeping the battlefields to the east of the road and in control of Kasaba/Drinjaca road. And notes that: "We have no one to appoint from the Drina Corps command to do this." In the second paragraph he notes that: "If you agree with this proposal, send a telegram of confirmation to the commands of the 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade, the 1st Milici Light Infantry Brigade, and the Zvornik CSB centre." And in the third paragraph he informs the commander what he's proposing to do with the number of soldiers with respect to the Zepa operation. And as you can see reflected, the coms centre and the Bratunac Brigade processed this at 15 July 1995 at 1615 hours. Of course here is the original.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Butler, it appears in this proposal he has volunteered Mr. Blagojevic to command all these units and he has done it apparently from the Bratunac Brigade. Can you -- what can you conclude, if anything, about that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, with respect to that individual piece, from a military perspective I have to presume that Colonel Milanovic discussed the issue with Mr. Blagojevic before recommending him for that task.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why is that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be very unusual and it certainly wouldn't be the proper function of a staff officer to make a recommendation or a proposal that subsequently would not be able to be carried out. As a matter of military professionalism on the part of staff officers, you don't make proposals that you know aren't going to be able to be executed. So as a matter of military common sense, as you will, one would not expect Colonel Milanovic to make this proposal if he did not already believe that Colonel Blagojevic would agree to the proposal or would be incapable of carrying it out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to the next document then. I believe it's 496. Regular combat report from the Bratunac Brigade, 16 July. Can you point out the relevant portion of this.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: With respect to paragraph 1, the enemy forces, I would direct your attention to the last sentence where it notes that from statements taken from enemy soldiers, there are about 2.000 in the wider area of the village of Pobudje and I believe the Court is familiar where that is located on the map at this point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remind me.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: My apologies. That village complex is located in this general area here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right under where it says Nova Kasaba.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Or right to the west of -- or the east of Nova Kasaba.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. And what else?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In paragraph 2, it notes what their forces are doing and reflects the fact that a MUP unit was pulled out this morning from the Kravica/Konjevic Polje direction, that the Bratunac Brigade had to dispatch a company to block that direction. It reflects that on the 16th of July they're making preparations to dispatch two additional companies of 100 soldiers to the Zvornik Infantry brigade or as they say, Light Infantry Brigade, as well as elements of the 4th Reconnaissance Platoon of the 1st Battalion. The next sentence indicates that during the day the brigade commander visited all units which are blocking the enemy retreat, and they're listed as being the 1st Milici Light Infantry Brigade, units of the 65th Motorised Protection Regiment, which is in this instance is the military police battalion, parts of the MUP, and the 5th Engineering Battalion, define their tasks and organise their joints acts and communications. Finally it reflects that because of the engagement of forces of the Bratunac 1st Light Infantry Brigade and the 1st Milici Light Infantry Brigade on other task assignments, execution of the task of searching the terrain has been slowed down, and actions to block enemy forces in the aforementioned area have been hampered. From the communications centre stamp, this document was handled by them at 1640 on 16 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you relate this -- any part of this document to the previous proposal of Mr. Milanovic?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This indicates that the proposal was accepted by the corps commander, and that Colonel Blagojevic was, in fact, put in command of all these forces from these units that were sweeping the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: One more issue on this, if I can direct the Court's attention to the handwritten version of this document. You'll note a considerable amount of scratch outs as this document was being drafted, however, I would draw your attention to the signature down here under the signature block, again the signature I've come to recognise as that of being Colonel Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's go on to the next exhibit. I believe it's 497. And going in the chronology, can you remind us what this is and what you wanted to talk about here for the 16th.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document, as previously discussed, is the reports and meetings book from the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade. That document where notes from the meetings of the command and command staff are jotted down. I draw the Court's attention to this one, the notations for a meeting on 16 July 1995, where it is evident that the commander is informing the commander and his corps command staff that he has just received an order to form a battalion for operations at Zepa by 0700 hours on 17 July 1995. And he is designating the 1st Battalion will be that battalion as well as a small anti-tank detachment. And finally, reflecting that they'll give battalion commander the orders during that evening or during the evening of 16th July in this instance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And let's go to 499, that we again recognise as a page out of the Bratunac military --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Your microphone, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you. I forgot I turned it off.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, this appears to be a page of the Bratunac MP log dated 17 July. And what is significant in this?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this respect, it notes that patrols are continuing on the apprehension and securing of Muslims in the municipal areas of Bratunac and Srebrenica. And it further indicates that one police patrol remained in Pilica to secure and guard the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you have any indication from documents or intercepts or -- of the fate of any Muslims that were apprehended by the MPs on this date, in the Bratunac area?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Specifically by the MPs, no, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And we've heard about the Pilica before, so let's just go on to the next exhibit that you've chosen and you have, is it 268?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this is a 17 July intercept and can you tell us why you've chosen this. What's significant? What do you find in this intercept that's significant?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this particular intercept at 1220 hours, there's a conversation from Badem, which is of course the headquarters of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade, and Micic, the operations officer from that brigade is talking to an unknown correspondent. And clearly from the text you can hear it's not a very good line and there's some confusion between Micic and Trisic. And finally, he clarifies that by saying M. Mostar In the context of the conversation Micic is letting this unknown correspondent know that 400 have set off at 1130 hours in seven buses and reflects that Blagojevic is at the head and Micic knows that he'll be leaving with the last one. For me, the significance of this is that at this point in time, Colonel Blagojevic is leaving the Bratunac Brigade zone at the head of this battalion and will be engaged in combat activities related to Zepa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So do you relate this back to the previous documents on the same subject?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: With respect to the formation of that battalion, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next exhibit, which I believe is 500. It appears to be a Main Staff document with the signature block under the commander Ratko Mladic coming in to the 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade. What is this?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, given the absence of the brigade commander and as discussed earlier the absence of the Bratunac Brigade chief of staff on combat operations, there's a significant shortage of commanders left in and around this area who can do some functions. As indicated earlier, there were no Drina Corps officers who could perform this task. In response to this situation, the Main Staff directs that on 17 July, the forces of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade, the Milici Light Infantry Brigade, the 67th Communications Battalion -- I'm sorry, the 67th Military Police Battalion. Let me read this again, 67th Communications Regiment and the Military Police Battalion of the 65th Motorised Protection Regiment and MUP forces will continue their operations, but that the Main Staff is appointing Lieutenant Colonel Keserovic an officer from the military police of the Main Staff security administration as the commander of these forces during the conduct of the tasks. It notes that the deadline for the completion of these tasks is 19 July 1995. And it also notes that Colonel Keserovic is required to propose an order for further engagement towards Cerska on 19 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this task related to the task that Mr. Blagojevic was doing the previous day as outlined in the Bratunac daily combat report?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This 67th communications group, is this the first time we hear about them?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where they come into this?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 67th Communications Regiment is the communications regiment for the Main Staff of the VRS. It is not a combat formation. But apparently in this particular case, given the extreme shortage of manpower a composite unit was put together from even that formation and thrown into the battle area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this paragraph 3 suggest in any way that the Main Staff has taken over direct command of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: They have not taken over direct command of the Bratunac Brigade. It does specify that they're in charge or he's in command of the forces during the conduct of the task. That means that those forces that are engaged in the sweep operation will fall under his direct command. It's not Colonel Blagojevic or Major Nastic or any of the other unit commanders relinquishing command of their units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell us briefly about what paragraphs 1 and 2 relate to, as I know we're coming up to the Zvornik area soon, hopefully.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Paragraphs 1 and 2 reflect another series of officers who were sent to the zone of the Zvornik Brigade responsibility to assist the command in planning and coordinating combat operations. Looking at this in context, on 17 July 1995, the brigade commander of the Zvornik Brigade, Colonel Pandurevic, has already allowed the column to pass through. And as the history part indicates, he was not authorised to do that. That was a decision that he, in fact, made on his own. These three officers from the Main Staff were sent, my understanding is, by General Miletic to write a report about this situation and that this report was to be provided to General Mladic. In the greater context, when you read the 18 July interim combat report from Colonel Pandurevic, it is in part in response to this commission coming down and investigating his activities. And it is his response to the corps commander, General Krstic, that he expects the corps commander's support in this matter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next exhibit. It should be 501. Tell us what this is.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a document from the command of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade to the Drina Corps command, noting that the brigade among the Muslim prisoners that the brigade has captured that day, there are four underaged children, and it lists their age, who are being held in military custody in Bratunac. It notes that one of them told the commander of the unit who was searching the area about the large number of Muslim troops committing suicide or killing each other. And that the author, we, the brigade, propose that this testimony be recorded by cameras from your press centre, that being the Drina Corps press centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, these four children, can you briefly relate what you believe their capture is related to, any particular operation by any individuals in the area.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that these four individuals we know from various investigations and interviews that a group of Bratunac Brigade soldiers was searching the greater Pobudje area on 17 July and had captured a number of prisoners, among them these four individuals.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were Bratunac working with another unit on that, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were working with the MUP.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And did these four children survive, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is my understanding that these four children survived. If we can examine the handwritten version of that, we'll notice on the B/C/S version that it was processed very late on the night of 18 July -- very early in the morning of 18 July at approximately 0010 hours -- no, I'm sorry 0040 hours. And this is the original handwritten version. And there is no signature to indicate the officer who signed this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And would you go to the next exhibit you've chosen, 502, if you've got it.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is also from the command of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade on 17 July, and again reflected in the communications centre stamp, that it was not processed until 0040 hours on the 18th of July. Again to the Drina Corps noting that the brigade command does not have at its disposal a single vehicle or motor vehicle suitable for transport of wounded Muslim prisoners from the Bratunac health centre to Bijeljina. It requests the command send a suitable vehicle for transport of the 23 wounded Muslim prisoners.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are these the prisoners you've spoken of before in part?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, they are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as far as you know, they all survived?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you make anything from these various documents on whether -- who signed it or authored it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again -- I will reserve a judgement on the handwriting comparison, but certainly it's the same situation as the last one. There is no signature to indicate which officer would have signed it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next exhibit, I believe it's 503. It appears to be an 18 July daily combat report from Bratunac. What's significant about this?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just as part of the overall situation, paragraph 1 reflecting that the Bratunac Brigade command is still aware of small enemy groups retreating in the area of Pobudje in Konjevic Polje in the direction of Cerska and Kuslat towards Tuzla noting that on that day units of the 3rd Infantry Battalion, the 4th Infantry Battalion and people mobilised from compulsory labour are searching the terrain. And again it was processed through at 1620 hours on 18 July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is there any indication that Mr. Blagojevic signed or drafted this document?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if Mr. Blagojevic left the head of the column on the 17th towards Zepa, can you tell us when or where you think he is on the days following the 17th.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on my reading of the continuation of Bratunac Brigade daily combat reports for the rest of the month of July, while he may well have made occasional trips back to Bratunac, I believe that he spends the majority of his time dealing with the situation with Zepa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that affect his responsibility over the command of his brigade?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. In effect, it's the same situation that we talk about with Colonel Vinko Pandurevic. When he and his battle group goes from the Zvornik Brigade to the zone of the Bratunac Brigade to be involved in the operations at Srebrenica. Colonel Blagojevic, as in the case of Colonel Pandurevic, is not formally relinquishing command of their unit. However, it is understood that the appointed deputy is going to be the person in charge of day-to-day operations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next document, 504. And tell us what this document is, where it came from, and what you find significant about it.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document, again from the command of the 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade intelligence organ to the Main Staff intelligence sector and the command of the Drina Corps intelligence sector. And it reflects that at 1515 hours on 18 July, 22 wounded Muslim prisoners from the 28th Division were evacuated with a police escort provided by the Drina Corps from the health centre and their destination is ultimately the Batkovici prisoner of war camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this is under the name of Momir Nikolic. Are you familiar with Mr. Nikolic's testimony on this point?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who do you think the author of this document was?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we can go to the last page of the B/C/S draft version, we see the same initials that are on the 13 July 1995 report under the name of Colonel Radoslav Jankovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Is there anything else you want to comment on this document?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Finally for this segment about Bratunac, let's go to Exhibit 505. Again, it's a page out of the meetings of the Bratunac Brigade that we've become familiar with. And if you could go to October 16th. Now, first of all, can you from your -- in your opinion, can you tell us who was present at this working meeting of the command with command staff and battalion commanders.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel Blagojevic is listed. Major Nikolic is listed. Lieutenant Micic, who of course is an operations officer. Major Trisic, who is the assistant commander for rear services of the brigade. I don't know the identity of M. Cvetinovic. P. Jovanovic is the acting commander of the 2nd Infantry Battalion at the time. I believe Beatovic is the acting commander of -- let me back off that one. I'm not familiar with that one. Petrovic is the acting commander of the 3rd Battalion and Ostojic is the battalion commander of the 1st Battalion. And at this period in time the 4th Battalion, which is normally associated during July 1995 with the Bratunac Brigade, has been resubordinated back to the Zvornik Infantry Brigade, so they don't have that as their 4th Battalion anymore.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what in this is significant to the historical events that are going on at the time?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The observations listed under Nikolic, noting that they're trying to block the village of Slapovic today and trying to catch remaining Turks, who should be there according to the statement of detainees, reflecting the fact that the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade has seven.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the investigation, to your knowledge, able to determine the fate of those seven?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, it has. And I understand that the seven, in fact, did survive the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. What's next?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It also notes at the last bullet that we are currently engaged in tasks issued by the Army of Republika Srpska. It's General staff, it should be Main Staff, and sanitation. And if I can go to the original B/C/S version of this. The phrase reflected is one we are accustom to, "asanacija," which is the phrase associated with the burial of the dead bodies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So are you aware of any photographic and forensic evidence that would relate to this statement about asanacija?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Within the context of the time involved, what I know to be occurring on the basis of that information, is that the elements of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade and other elements of the civilian protection are involved in the process of exhuming the primary mass grave at Glogova and is installing the remains from that grave in seven identified secondary -- or six identified secondary graves and one grave that we call a tertiary grave because the remains were moved from that for a third time. So this, in context, is related to the process of robbing the bodies out of the mass grave that was established at Glogova and dispersing the bodies in hidden sites along the road to Zeleni Jadar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Just a minor clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The gentleman was asked if he's aware of any photographic or forensic evidence and he then began to give an explanation of something that was not in concert with the question that was posed. Do they have a yes or no -- I would prefer him answering the question as opposed to him giving a rendition to what he thinks we all should know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, I think this question should be asked during the cross-examination, but we still have two minutes left. Maybe Mr. McCloskey could ask some questions to this witness so that we could get a complete record of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, the reason I raise the objection at this point is because at some point I anticipate cross-examining and I would appreciate if the witness would be responding to my questions as opposed to giving lectures.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I can see we're getting ready for cross-examination already, and I certainly hope we can tone down the rhetoric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, can you help me out on this. Can you answer the question about the photographs?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I'm quite familiar with overhead imagery provided by the United States government which reflects the activity of the opening and the removal of bodies from Glogova and the installation of the secondary graves in Zeleni Jadar. I am familiar with the activities of the investigation team with respect to the OTP's activity in exhuming those graves and the forensics involved around them. And I am familiar with the interviews by members of the OTP with individuals who participated in that operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, this does end the presentation of this evidence on the Bratunac area. Just to give you -- if we're lucky, we may get through Zvornik tomorrow. We may go into Monday a little bit, but certainly the Prosecution doesn't anticipate going very far into Monday on its direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, thank you very much. It's time for the break. So we'll break now and resume tomorrow morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
